column1: Create Initial Version of GUI SDD
column34:
*Two-part effort*:
1. Discovery - figure out what's actually needed in SDD documentation
2. Automation - build tooling to generate SDD docs automatically

*current documentation flow*:
*SRS -> drives design/implementation of code -> SDD

*The problem*: 
SDDs are subject to the PTR/CCB process for any change. That creates a mismatch; code evolves constantly, but SDD changes carry process overhead. The fix os to make the SDD generic enough that routine code changes don't force PTR/CCB. It should stay a high-level document that gves the customer enough understanding without gating day-to-day development. 

*Steps*:
* How to make storybook exclude certain content for certian builds
* How to run storybook statically
* Add stories for non visual components 
* GUI architecture with external interfaces

I would like to visualize the ROV catenary in a rendered 3D animation on the MAM page/screen of the the SSW GUI,

so I can have supported situational awareness of the the predictive real-time state of the ROV catenary in the water column.

{*}+Description+{*}:
 * This story involves creating a standalone front-end component that will render the real-time 3D representation of the state of the ROV catenary. 
 ** The resulting component will be incorporated into the MAM page

{+}*Acceptance Criteria*{+}:

GIVEN I have the MAM screen open on the ROV workstation,

WHEN there is a change in the position of the deployed ROV,

THEN I will see a change in the 3D visualization of of the ROV catenary.

{+}*UI/UX Notes*{+}:
 * library for creating the 3D render needs to be determined in this story or preceding task/spike under this story's Epic
 ** determine whether there is a separate application with rendering created by another EB team that already exists for catenary

{+}*Technical Notes*{+}:
 * Testing this component will require that we have a reliable mock application or library for providing data for updating the 3D animation
 ** If this is a separate application and not a model provided via library, we will need a network interface for receiving data

*Summary:*

Our current CI/CD process is not staged (i.e.: all lints/tests are ran on every development merge). Moving forward, we would like to speed up the iteration process for developers by separating out levels of testing and mapping them to different branches. This means that acceptance tests will run on merges to integration, and errors will be kicked back in the form of new tasks. Developers will only need to verify to the unit/functional level (can manually run acceptance tests if updating/implementing them). Staging will also allow us to implement a pre-release versioning scheme that maps to the larger project CI/CD process.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Slow merge process into development

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Updates our versioning scheme and mapped level of confidence to be aligned with the larger project

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Create prototype CI/CD design
 * Implement each stage in a feature branch
 * Merge the feature branch, go through the process, and fix bugs

As an operator ,

I want/need the front-end design of the tabs for the groups for calibration controls to be visually and behaviorally consistent across the different SSW subsystem GUIS,

so that overall mental load is reduced and I can readily understand how the calibration controls work across different GUIs.

 * Design, implement, unit and acceptance test the common Tabs Calibration Component.
 * Finalize and write corresponding ESTAP GUI SRS and TCAP GUI SRS requirements.

{+}*Acceptance Criteria*{+}:

GIVEN the Common Tabs Calibration Component is implemented,

WHEN an operator interacts with the component,

THEN they will be able to freely switch between calibration component tabs and interact with calibration buttons.

{+}*UI/UX Notes*{+}:
 * The component needs to be designed with parameters that allow for practically any number of calibration control groups (tabs) and controls to populate the rendered component.

{+}*Technical Notes*{+}:
 * Dependent on the Common Pop-up Confirmation Component

so that while running the GUI on the tactical system I can adjust calibration values to support SSW operations.

 * Finalize and write corresponding TCAP GUI SRS requirements.

{+}*Acceptance Criteria*{+}:

THEN the GUI successfully renders the page with a layout based on the front-end design.

so that while running the GUI on the tactical system I can adjust calibration values to support SSW operations.

I want/need a confirmation pop-up to be rendered when I issue a calibration order,

so that I do not unintentionally order calibration for a control system sensor.

Using this component, an operator will be able to order the tray to move vertically and horizontally in the ESTCS deployment scope. Additionally, should cable deployment for the L/L motors fall out-of-sync, the operator will be able to control the L/L Forward or Aft motors separately.

Summary:

The ESTAP GUI is what the operator uses to control the movement of the tray. It is responsible for providing the visuals needed to for operators to conduct SSW mission operations. The ESTAP GUI allows operators to view the live status of the External Stowage Tray (EST). 

The TCAP GUI is what the operator uses to control the movement of the tube 9 and tube 10 hatches. It is responsible for providing the visuals needed to for operators to conduct SSW mission operations. The TCAP GUI allows operators to view the live status of the Tube Control System (TCS). It also allows operators to move the tube hatches and override sensor values. The purpose of this milestone is to document the design, implement and test the Electronic Circuit Breakers unit of TCAP GUI.
